body.text: A 19-year-old woman is critical, and three men are in serious but stable conditions, after a shooting south of Brisbane.
Fitzy's Loganholme was hosting a boxing event when multiple shots were fired from a vehicle just after 8pm.
Police are searching for multiple perpetrators but do not believe there is any further threat to the community.
A woman is in a critical condition and three men are seriously injured after a drive-by shooting south of Brisbane.
Police were called to Fitzy's on Bryants Road in Loganholme just after 8pm on Saturday after reports of shots fired from a vehicle.

Inspector Galpin says a group of people gathered in the passenger drop-off zone at the pub during an intermission.
"At 8:15pm a Mitsubishi motor vehicle approached the drop-off zone, stopping in close proximity to those outside," he says.
"A number of shots were then fired from the front passenger window of that vehicle, striking four persons."
He says CCTV and witnesses captured two men in the vehicle both wearing balaclavas and gloves.
Inspector Galpin says the investigation is in its infancy.
He says a local boxing gym held its annual pro-am boxing event at Fitzy's Loganholme.
"The event has been advertised on social media for about two months," he says.
He says the owners of the gym are cooperating with police.
"[They] did not receive any information to suggest an incident like this may occur."
Detective Inspector Ian Galpin has offered his condolences to the victims.

"This is a horrific incident, and I wish to ensure the family and the friends of those who are injured and the community as a whole that the QPS are committed to identifying those persons invovled and bringing them before the court," he says.
Good morning. Queensland Police are giving an update to media following a drive-by shooting south of Brisbane.
A 19-year-old woman is in a critical condition, and three men are seriously injured, after shots were fired from a vehicle at Fitzy's Loganholme last night.
A 19-year-old woman has been taken to hospital in a life-threatening condition, where she has undergone emergency surgery.
Three men, aged 27, 37 and 38, were also taken to hospital where they remain in a serious but stable condition.
Police said a silver Mitsubishi believed to have been involved was found on Maloney Road in Waterford West a short time later, and they are searching for a second vehicle and multiple perpetrators.
The venue was hosting a boxing event for Logan City Titles.
Local community left reeling
Premier David Crisafulli said Queensland would react to the shooting with "sorrow, anger, with a resolve to want to get to the bottom of it".

"It's just completely unacceptable that people on a night out at a pub doing something as Queenslander as you can possibly find can be caught and find themselves as collateral damage in such a horrendous, horrendous crime," Mr Crisafulli said.
He said his government had passed "the strongest new laws" for drive-by shootings in the country.
"People shouldn't be out on a night out and have to second guess whether or not the next car that's driving by them might be firing bullets and raining bullets at them."
Logan mayor Jon Raven said the attack had "sent a shockwave" through the city.
"We've never seen anything like this happen in our city before," he said.
"I know that there was lots of children who were there last night; this is going to impact them for the rest of their lives."
Local resident Shae Hilton said the attack had left her "absolutely gobsmacked".
"This place has been such a family place for so long and seeing this has actually put goosebumps through my body," she said.
"It makes me sick knowing even just young people were involved. Young people shouldn't be involved in things like this."
In a statement, Logan City Titles said they were "praying for full recoveries".
"As a team we are working through it and dealing with the emotions that come with this.
"Right now our thoughts go out to the victims and all that were affected."
Investigations are underway and police said they did not believe there was any further threat to the public.
